Quantum Angle GeneratorPrivate repositoryarXiv ↗
Angle encoding of random inputs, a parametrized unitary, and one expectation value per qubit decoded into the energy of one cell.
06
Other Generative Models
Classical generative models for calorimeter simulation, the multi universal approximator (one independent qubit per pixel, no entanglement), and four quantum generative models for calorimeter showers developed with Jamal Slim: the coherent memory register, QFAN, the interferometric QPCE and the compiled IQP Born machine.
Show 5 sections ▾
Multi Universal ApproximatorGitHub ↗
One independent single-qubit universal approximator per output (pixel), all sharing the same input noise, without any entangling gate.
Coherent Memory RegisterGitHub ↗ arXiv ↗
In each round a unitary entangles a work register with a memory register. The work register is measured to give one component of the sample, while the memory is never measured and carries the correlations between rounds.
Quantum Feature Amplification NetworkGitHub ↗ arXiv ↗
An autoregressive model: every step runs the same circuit, with encoding angles computed from the pixels already generated, and a linear decoder turns the measured parities into the next block of pixels.
Interferometric Quantum Polynomial Chaos ExpansionGitHub ↗ arXiv ↗
Noise germs are re-uploaded at the start of every block of an interferometer, so the depth sets the order of the chaos expansion. One expectation value per qubit gives the energy of one calorimeter cell.
Compiled IQP Born MachineGitHub ↗ arXiv ↗
An IQP Born machine for calorimeter images at 64 qubits. The mixture of IQP circuits is compiled into a single IQP circuit with a few ancilla qubits.
07
Pauli Propagation for Quantum Machine Learning
Symbolic Pauli propagation in the Heisenberg picture, used for gradient-enabled classical pre-training of parametrized quantum circuits ahead of deployment on hardware.
Show 1 section ▾
Pauli-PropagatorGitHub ↗ arXiv 2512.16674 ↗arXiv 2610.32571 ↗
Propagate the observable, minimize the resulting loss classically, then deploy the trained circuit on hardware.
